chunks: 5187 - Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There were some children in the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام playing with their arrows. One of them threw his arrow and broke his companion’s front tooth. That was brought to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and the thrower established proof that he had said, ‘Beware!’ So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام waived qiṣāṣ from him, then said:
The one who warned has excused himself.

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةَ: legal proof or evidence presented to establish a claim
key_terms.الْقِصَاصَ: retaliatory legal retribution for bodily injury
key_terms.حَذَارِ: beware; a warning given to avoid harm
key_terms.رَبَاعِيَةَ: a front tooth, specifically the incisor next to the central teeth
key_terms.قَدْ أَعْذَرَ مَنْ حَذَّرَ: a legal maxim meaning that one who gave warning has fulfilled his excuse

ai.seo_question: Does giving a clear warning remove liability for accidental injury in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a legal judgment from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning an injury caused during children’s play. Because the boy who caused the injury had given a prior warning and established that with evidence, qiṣāṣ was removed from him, expressing the principle that one who duly warns has discharged responsibility in such a case.
